### Observed differences

- The two windows show essentially swapped participation for two activity blocks. A21, A22 and A23 each appeared in about 19 in 100 traces in the earlier window and about 79 in 100 in the later window, while A24, A25 and A26 each fell from about 82 in 100 traces to about 21 in 100. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- At the branch point A20, which occurs in every trace in both windows, the outgoing transitions moved from roughly 82% leading to A24, A25 or A26 (about 19% to A21–A23) in the earlier window to roughly 79% leading to A21, A22 or A23 (about 21% to A24–A26) in the later window. [DIR003]
- The two blocks were mutually exclusive in both windows: traces containing one block almost never contain the other (co-occurrence about 1 in 100 or less). Within the block that executes, the three activities now usually occur together — A21 and A22 co-occurred in about 19 in 100 traces before versus 79 in 100 after — with no fixed order between them (both orders in roughly equal shares). [REL015, REL017, REL023, REL024]
- Downstream activities switched which block they accompany. A30 co-occurred with A24–A26 in about 82 in 100 traces before and with A21–A23 in about 19 in 100; afterwards these shares reversed (about 79 in 100 with A21–A23, about 21 with A24–A26). A32 and A33 co-occurred with A21–A23 in about 9 in 100 traces before versus about 55 in 100 after, and with A24–A26 in about 52 in 100 before versus about 15 in 100 after. [REL020, REL027, REL038, REL045, REL021, REL039]
- A10 became rarer (about 17 in 100 traces before, 7 after), appears at an earlier event position (median about 0.86 versus 0.36 of the trace), and its outgoing transitions spread from almost exclusively A33 (about 97%) across several activities; the later-window side rests on only about 14 observed transitions. [POS001, DIR002, LAG001]
- A02 rose from about 2 to 9 in 100 traces with a completely redistributed successor profile, backed by only 4 versus 18 observations. [OCC001, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a large shift in how often two existing alternative paths are taken. In the earlier window, about 82 in 100 traces executed the block A24–A26 after A20, and about 19 in 100 executed the alternative block A21–A23; in the later window this reversed to about 79 in 100 for A21–A23 and about 21 in 100 for A24–A26. The shift is visible directly in A20's outgoing transitions, both blocks and all involved activities were observed in substantial shares in both windows, the blocks remained mutually exclusive, and the internal structure of the executing block (three activities together, no fixed order) is unchanged. Downstream, A30 and A32/A33 now typically run with A21–A23 instead of A24–A26, consistent with following whichever block executes. [DIR003, OCC002, OCC005, REL009, REL012, REL015, REL017, REL020, REL021, REL038]

This goes beyond what chance sampling would produce: 60 control-flow items qualified against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed, and the qualifying items agree in direction across occurrence, routing and relation indicators, with the main activities backed by roughly 37–200 traces per window. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the routing rule itself did not change but the two windows contain different mixes of two pre-existing case types; both would produce the observed pattern. [OCC002, OCC005, DIR003, REL009, REL012, REL020, REL038]

Other differences: A10 became rarer (about 17 in 100 traces before, 7 after), appears at an earlier event position, and its outgoing transitions spread from almost exclusively A33 to several activities; A02 became slightly more frequent (about 2 to 9 in 100 traces) with redistributed successors. Both rest on few observations (A10: 33 versus 14 transitions; A02: 4 versus 18) and are not part of the main hypothesis. [POS001, DIR002, LAG001, OCC001, DIR001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Screening: 180 units tested, 60 items qualified, 0.9 expected without change. The control_flow family: 180 units tested, 60 items, 0.9 expected. So 60 items vs 0.9 expected — that's many times larger than the chance expectation. This cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past the screening comparison and judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Now let me understand the behavioural pattern.

OCC items:
- OCC001: A02 participation 0.02 → 0.09 (2% → 9% of traces). Support 4 → 18. Small numbers, weak.
- OCC002: A21 participation 0.19 → 0.79 (19% → 79%). Support 38 → 158.
- OCC003: A22 participation 0.185 → 0.79. Support 37 → 158.
- OCC004: A23 participation 0.185 → 0.795. Support 37 → 158.
- OCC005: A24 participation 0.815 → 0.21. Support 163 → 42.
- OCC006: A25 participation 0.815 → 0.21. Support 163 → 42.
- OCC007: A26 participation 0.82 → 0.21. Support 164 → 42.

So A21, A22, A23 became much more frequent (from ~19% to ~79% of traces), while A24, A25, A26 became much less frequent (from ~82% to ~21%). This looks like a swap: a group of three activities (A21–A23) replaced another group (A24–A26) in about 60% of traces.

DIR003: A20's outgoing transitions redistributed. Before: A25 0.24, A22 0.085, A26 0.285, A24 0.29, A21 0.07, A23 0.03. After: A23 0.29, A25 0.08, A22 0.215, A21 0.285, A24 0.07, A26 0.06. So from A20, transitions to A24/A25/A26 dominated before (0.29+0.24+0.285 = 0.815), and transitions to A21/A22/A23 dominated after (0.285+0.215+0.29 = 0.79). Support 200 in both windows — A20 occurs in all traces.

REL009–REL014 (A20 vs A21–A23): before, A20 co-occurs with A21 in only 19% of traces (A_only 81%); after, co-occurrence 79%. Similarly for A22, A23. Conversely REL012–REL014 (A20 vs A24–A26): before co-occurrence ~82%, after ~21%.

REL015–REL016 (A21 vs A22, A21 vs A23): before, neither 81% (they rarely occur in same trace); after, co-occurrence 79%, with A_before_B ~0.37–0.395 and B_before_A ~0.375–0.395 — both orders in similar proportions, so no fixed order between them. REL023 (A22 vs A23): same pattern.

REL017–REL019 (A21 vs A24–A26): before, B_only 81% (A24–A26 occur without A21); after, A_only 79% (A21 occurs without A24–A26). So A21 and A24–A26 are now alternatives — they almost never co-occur.

REL024–REL026 (A22 vs A24–A26): same. REL030–REL032 (A23 vs A24–A26): same.

REL036–REL037, REL041 (A24 vs A25, A24 vs A26, A25 vs A26): before co-occurrence ~82% (they occurred together, in both orders — A_before_B 0.465, B_before_A 0.335, so mixed order); after, neither 79% (they rarely occur in the same trace at all).

REL020, REL027, REL033 (A21/A22/A23 vs A30): before, B_only ~81% (A30 occurred without A21–A23); after, co-occurrence 79% with A_before_B ~0.44–0.45 and interleaved ~0.34. So A30 now usually occurs together with A21–A23.

REL038, REL042, REL045 (A24/A25/A26 vs A30): before co-occurrence ~82%; after B_only ~79% (A30 occurs without A24–A26).

REL021, REL022, REL028, REL029, REL034, REL035 (A21–A23 vs A32/A33): before, B_only ~52%, co-occurrence ~9%; after, co-occurrence ~55%, B_only ~15%. So A21–A23 now usually co-occur with A32/A33.

REL039, REL040, REL043, REL044, REL046, REL047 (A24–A26 vs A32/A33): before co-occurrence ~52%; after B_only ~55%. Reversed.

REL001–REL003 (A10 vs A21–A23): before, A_only 12.5–13%, B_only 15%, neither 68.5%; after, B_only 73.5%, neither 19.5%. So A10 now usually occurs without A21–A23... wait, B_only means A21–A23 occur without A10. Before, A10 and A21–A23 rarely co-occurred (cooccurrence 3.5–4%); after, still low cooccurrence (5.5%) but B_only jumped to 73.5% because A21–A23 now occur in 79% of traces while A10 occurs in only 7%.

REL004–REL006 (A10 vs A24–A26): before, B_only 68.5% (A24–A26 occurred without A10, cooccurrence 13%); after, neither 73.5% (neither occurs — A10 dropped to 7% and A24–A26 dropped to 21%).

DIR002: A10's outgoing transitions. Before: A33 0.97 (97% to A33), A32 0.03. After: spread across A15 0.214, A35 0.071, A33 0.143, A14 0.071, A20 0.071, A16 0.143, A27 0.143, A34 0.143. Support 33 → 14. A10 participation dropped from 16.5% to 7% (POS001 support). So A10 became rarer and its outgoing transitions changed from almost always A33 to a spread. But support is small (33 and 14 outgoing transitions), so this is weakly supported.

POS001: A10 position moved from median ~0.86 to median ~0.36, std increased. Support 33 → 14. Position-based, weak support.

DIR001: A02's outgoing transitions. Before: A11 0.5, A20 0.25, A01 0.25 (support 4). After: spread over 10 targets (support 18). Very few observations — weak.

This is consistent with "existing paths are taken with different frequencies" — a routing share shift. Both blocks are observed in substantial shares in both windows (19% and 82% before; 79% and 21% after). Hmm, 19% — is that substantial? It's about 38 of 200 traces. I'd say it's a substantial minority. The condition says "observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows". 19% vs 82%... The shift is from roughly 1-in-5 to 4-in-5. Then judge by directness, consistency, ability to rule out competing explanations. The OCC, DIR003, and REL009–REL047 items all consistently describe one underlying difference: a swap in which mutually exclusive block executes. The support counts are large (37–164 traces per window for the main activities; 200 for A20 relations). Empirical strength 0.995 for all items. The pattern is highly consistent across many pairwise relations.

Competing explanations: Could this be a sampling fluctuation? A shift from 19% to 79% with 200 traces per window — the empirical strength (99.5% of reference comparisons smaller) plus the screening count comparison addresses chance. The screening says 60 items qualified when 0.9 expected — the count is many times larger, so chance as a whole can't explain it.
